metadata.title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums

problem_summary.summary: Return k pairs formed from one value in each sorted input array, ordered by nondecreasing pair sum.
problem_summary.input_output: Inputs: non-decreasing integer arrays nums1 and nums2, and k. Return k value pairs with the smallest sums; equal-valued pairs from different positions are retained.
constraints: Both arrays are sorted in non-decreasing order

brute_force.explanation: Generate every index pair, sort all pairs by their summed values, and return the first k. This is a simple exhaustive baseline, but its product-sized memory use makes it unsuitable for large arrays.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every possible pair is generated exactly once. Sorting by sum places the globally smallest pairs first, so taking the first k returns the requested set of pairs, including ties as separate index combinations.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(P log P), where P = nums1.length * nums2.length, for generating and sorting every pair.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(P) auxiliary for all generated pairs, in addition to O(k) returned pairs.

optimized.explanation: Treat each nums1 index i as a sorted row of sums (nums1[i] + nums2[j]). Put the first pair of up to min(k, nums1.length) rows in a min-heap. Repeatedly remove the smallest pair and insert the next pair from that same row.
optimized.correctness_idea: Within a row, sums are nondecreasing because nums2 is sorted. The heap contains the smallest unreported pair from every active row, so its minimum is the smallest unreported pair globally. Advancing only the row that was removed enumerates pairs in nondecreasing sum order without visiting the full Cartesian product.
optimized.time_complexity: O(h log h + k log(h + 1)), where h = min(k, nums1.length), for heap initialization and at most k removals/insertions.
optimized.space_complexity: O(h) auxiliary for the heap, excluding O(k) returned pairs.

steps.event: Seed one pair from each of the three rows.
steps.action: Insert (i,0) for i = 0, 1, and 2; tuple state is [firstIndex, secondIndex, sum].

steps.event: Pop the globally smallest pair and advance its row.
steps.condition: The heap minimum is (nums1[0], nums2[0]) with sum 3.
steps.action: Append [1,2], then insert the next pair from row 0.

steps.event: Pop the next smallest pair and advance row 0 again.
steps.condition: The next heap minimum has sum 4.

steps.event: Pop from row 1 and advance to its next column.
Pop the fourth pair and finish.
steps.condition: The next minimum sum is 4 + 3 = 7; result now contains k pairs.
steps.action: Append [4,3] and stop without processing the remaining heap entries.

edge_cases.handling: The heap returns the pair formed by both arrays' first elements.
Distinct index pairs remain distinct outputs; the comparator uses indices only to make tie processing deterministic.

edge_cases.case: k exceeds the number of rows
edge_cases.handling: The heap starts with every nums1 row and advances rows as they are popped until k pairs are produced.
Sorted row monotonicity still holds, and sums are compared as long values.
